text:
The person wants to send an order back and get their money returned.
Send it back
I don't want this one anymore
Can I return these shoes and get a refund?
The jacket is too small, so how do I swap it for a bigger one?
The box came with a hole in the roof of it, so I'd like to send it back and ask for a new one.
Please start a return for the blue lamp and tell me when the courier will come.
I bought a set of plates and want to split it, keeping two and returning the other two.
This is my final try: could you please start the return for order 4471?

name: check_motion_alerts
does: Tells you what the motion sensors and cameras noticed while you were away.
inputs: which room or camera, and the time you want to know about
people say:
- Did anything move in the house today?
- Was somebody at the back door last night?
- I heard a strange noise, can you look at the cameras?
- The cleaning team was here this morning, but did anyone else come in?
- Something seemed to stir in the garden, was it just a cat?

The person wants to know which day the bins go out.
Bin day?
When do the bins go out?
Is it the recycling or the other one this week?
I should put the bins outside tonight, right?
Note to self: I keep forgetting the bins. Which night is it?
My neighbour's bin is already out and I'm all ear, so is it bin day for us too?
I just heard the lorry go by, did I miss it?
Could you please tell me which day the green bin goes to the kerb, so I can make a note of it?

Maya was a nurse, and her night shift at the hospital had been very long. She climbed into her car with tired eyes and a sore back. She did not want chatter or the news. She only wanted something soft.

"Quiet piano," she said to her phone.

The phone understood that she wanted gentle piano music at a low volume. It started a playlist called Calm Piano and turned the sound down a little so it would not wake her up more. Maya did not know the name of the first piece, but it was the kind she liked most after a hard night. It reminded her of a lullaby about a little horse that her grandmother used to hum.

She smiled, said thank you, and drove home slowly while the sun came up.

name: share_pickup_spot
does: Sends your driver a clear pickup spot and tells you when the car is close.
inputs: the address or landmark where you are standing, and which ride is yours
people say:
- Tell the driver where I'm standing
- He can't find me, I'm the one with a red coat and one green sock
- The main gate is broken, so ask him to meet me at the side door
- Let me know when the car is outside
- I'm by the big clock, can you send that to the driver?

Tomas was a cook, and the kitchen was busy. The oven was set to two hundred degrees, and his hands were covered in flour. He had forgotten something important. His dad's birthday was on Friday.

He tapped his phone with a knuckle and typed in a hurry: "remind me abuot dads birthday on friday and find a gift"

The phone understood the typo. It set a reminder for Friday morning called Dad's birthday. Then it showed a short list of gift ideas, such as a good pan, a book of recipes, or the usual box of tea from the market. Tomas liked the book. He knew his dad would want to practice making soup from it.

The assistant saved the idea in his notes, and Tomas went back to his onions.

The person wants to know how many ounces are in a number of grams.
Grams to ounces?
How many ounces is 250 grams?
What's 250 g in oz?
A banana weighs about 120 grams, so how many ounces is that?
I just installed a new kitchen scale and it only shows ounces, so what is 300 grams on it?
My recipe uses grams but my cups are old ones, so can you tell me how heavy 90 grams is in ounces?
I'm so proud of my first loaf of bread, and the recipe is in grams, so could you please tell me how many ounces a 500 gram bag of flour has? I would like to buy the right size.

Rosa owned a small hardware shop on the corner. It was a freezing morning, and she was still at home with a hot cup of tea. Her thoughts were on the shop.

"Remind me to call the supplier about the drill when I get to the shop," she said to her phone. "But don't set an alarm. I don't want anything loud."

The phone understood that she wanted a reminder, not an alarm. It asked what time she would arrive, and Rosa said she would come in around nine. The phone set a quiet note for nine o'clock that said Call the supplier about the drill. It made no sound and only showed the words on the screen.

When Rosa opened the shop, the note was waiting for her, and she made the call before the first customer came in.

Leo was eight years old, and he was making a paper chain for his room. It was a foggy morning, and he could not see the park from the window, so he sat at the table with his scissors and glue.

"Please could you tell me how many days are left until December twenty-fifth?" he asked the smart speaker. "I would like to know because I want to make one ring of paper for every day."

The speaker understood that Leo wanted a count of the days from today to the twenty-fifth of December. It counted them and said there were sixty-four days left. Leo wrote the number on a piece of paper, and the total looked very big.

"That is a lot of rings," he said. He asked his sister to help him cut.

The person wants to open the book at the page where they stopped.
Where was I?
Open my book at my bookmark.
Take me back to my page.
Continue reading.
I got a voicemail in the middle of my chapter and lost my place.
The story got so deep that I fell asleep, so which page was I on?
I laughed so hard at the last scene that I forgot where I stopped, can you find it?
Could you please open the book I was reading last night at the exact spot where I put the bookmark?

Sam was fifteen, and his bike chain kept slipping. He was hungry and waiting for dinner, so he picked up his phone and typed to the assistant.

"my bike chain is slipping. book a repair for saturday. no wait, sunday"

The assistant understood the change. It looked at the bike shops near his home and found one that was open on Sunday. It booked a slot at eleven in the morning and said so plainly: the repair was booked for Sunday at eleven, not Saturday.

Sam typed back that it was his birthday present to himself, and that he wanted the bike to begin the new year without a squeak. The assistant sent him a short message with the address of the shop and added the visit to his calendar.

A navigation app helps you get from one place to another. You say where you want to go, and it draws a route on the map and tells you how long the drive will take. The pale blue line on the screen is the way to go.

People often change the plan. Someone might say, add a stop at the pharmacy, or avoid the highway, or find me a faster way. A driver with a sore tooth might say, get me to the dentist by nine. The app also watches the traffic. If a road is slow, it may offer another way and tell you how many minutes you would save. People can say yes, keep the old way, or show me the next turn.

Dani was sixteen and sat on a bench in the park after school. Her phone was at ten percent, and she wished she knew why the house used so much power. The solar panels on the roof had a white box beside them that her dad was proud of.

She typed two words: "Power use?"

The assistant understood that she wanted to know how much electricity the house was using right now. It checked the home energy report and answered that the house was using a little less than usual, because the sun was out and the panels were making power. It also said the dryer was the biggest user at the moment.

Dani sent a quick message to her brother to turn the dryer off, and then put her phone away.

Ruth was not good with technology, but she wanted to send an invitation to her neighbours. She stood in the kitchen with her tablet. A frozen pie was baking in the oven, and a tap by the sink had a small leak that she meant to fix.

"Please fix the spelling in my invitation," she said slowly. "I think I spelled tomorrow wrong. The supper is tomorrow at seven."

The assistant understood that she had a short note and wanted it checked. It found the word tomorrow with the wrong letters and fixed it. Then it read the note back to her: Please come to supper tomorrow at seven. It said that it had fixed one word and left the rest as it was.

Ruth smiled, because it had been easy.

Person: can u book me a haircut
Assistant: Sure. Which day and what time would you like?
Person: tomorrow at seven
Assistant: The salon closes at six tomorrow. Would half past five work instead?
Person: ok. my hair looks like a jar of frozen spaghetti lol
Assistant: Then it is a good time for a trim. Do you want to choose a stylist, or should I pick whoever is free?
Person: whoever is free
Assistant: Done. You are booked for tomorrow at half past five.

The person wants the lamp at full brightness.
full brightness
turn the lamp all the way up
make the livng room lights as bright as they go
Lights at maximum, please.
It's dark as a rock cave in here.
I can't read this tiny print, can you make the lamp brighter?
The ceiling light as bright as it can be, please. I need to split these bills into piles.
Could you make the whole room as bright as possible? I'm looking for my keys.

Omar drove a delivery van, and his day had started before sunrise. He had already drunk a gallon of tea, and he still felt tired. At a red light, he spoke to the assistant in the van.

"Black coffee," he said.

The assistant understood that Omar wanted a hot black coffee, and that he wanted it on his way. It looked at the map and found a drive-through cafe two minutes down the road. It put the cafe on his route and told him it would be on the right.

Omar pulled in, and he watched the girl at the window pour the coffee into a paper cup. It was hot, and it was true to the name on the sign, strong and black. He thanked the assistant and went back to work.

name: estimate_wait_time
does: Tells you how long until a car can reach you and about what the ride will cost.
inputs: your pickup address and the kind of ride you want
people say:
- How long will I be waiting?
- Is there a car near me?
- The website says six minutes, is that true?
- Is it a long wait for a car at the station right now?
- Will it cost more now, since drivers earn extra at rush hour?

It was a busy morning, and Priya was driving her two children to school. The little ones were safe in their car seats, and for once they were quiet.

"Could you please play the next episode of my cooking podcast?" she asked the car assistant. "The kids are finally calm, and I would like to hear the end before I get to work."

The assistant understood that she wanted the podcast she had been listening to, and not a new one. It found the show, saw that she had stopped halfway through episode twelve, and started the next one. It said the title: how a baker sold his first hundred loaves.

Priya turned the sound up a little. She listened happily all the way to the school gate.

name: power_cut_helper
does: Tells you whether there is a power cut in your area and when the lights should come back on.
inputs: your address or postcode
people say:
- Why is it dark?
- Is the whole street out of power?
- When will the electricity come back?
- The fridge is getting warm, how long will this last?
- It's sunny and there's no storm, so why did the power go?
- The bank on the corner is dark too, is the whole town out?

Noor was seventeen, and she was going camping with friends on Friday. Her laundry was still in the dryer, and her bag was half packed. She typed to the assistant in a hurry.

"whats the wether at pine ridge this friday"

The assistant understood the spelling mistake. It looked up the forecast for Pine Ridge and said that Friday would be dry and sunny, with a cold night around four degrees. It suggested a warm hat and a second pair of socks.

Noor wrote back that she would enjoy a dry night for once, and that her friends were bringing the food. The assistant said it would be glad to add a packing list if she wanted one. She said yes, and thought about the delicious pancakes they would cook on the little stove.

The person wants to hear the news on the radio.
News on the radio.
Put on the news station.
Tune to the news, not the music.
I don't want songs right now, just the headlines.
I'm cutting the grass and want the news in my ears, but not the talk show.
It's a gray morning and I expect the traffic report is on soon, can you find it?
Switch the radio on and find something that tells me what is going on in town.
Would you mind tuning in to the news station? I would rather not hear the sports today.

Grandpa Walt sat in his armchair with a bottle of water in his hand. His little granddaughter had just helped him undo the cap, because his fingers were sore. The big game was on, but he had been out in the garden all afternoon.

"Who's winning?" he asked the speaker on the shelf.

The speaker understood that he meant the game his favourite team was playing right now. It looked up the match and said that the home team was ahead by two goals with ten minutes left.

Walt gave a happy shout. He asked the speaker to read out the score again when the game ended, and the speaker said it would tell him. His granddaughter sat down beside him to watch the end.

The person wants a reminder to read at a set time.
Reading time at seven.
Remind me to read tomorrow at seven.
Set aside half an hour for my book tonight.
It's rainy, so I'll stay in and read after dinner, can you remind me at eight?
Tell me when it's time for my chapter.
My book is by the stove, so call me at six to read it.
I need to read before I visit my aunt on Saturday morning, so remind me Friday at nine.
Please nudge me every evening around nine to read for a while, because I want to finish this book.

name: sort_my_waste
does: Tells you which bin an item goes in and what to do with it first.
inputs: the item, and what it is made of if you know
people say:
- Where does this pizza box go?
- Can I put an old scarf in the clothes bin?
- Is this glass jar okay for the blue bin?
- Where do I take old batteries?
- I want to move to a healthy zero-waste life, so what do I do with this plastic tray?

A bedtime routine tells your body that the day is over. Most people choose a time to go to bed and a time to wake up, and a phone or speaker can help with both. People say things like, wake me at six, give me ten more minutes, or no alarm on Sunday. They also say, turn the lights down, because a dark room helps you sleep.

A short nap is another way to rest. Someone might say, wake me in twenty minutes. A sleep tracker looks at how much you move in the night and tells you in the morning how well you slept. You can ask, how did I sleep? You can set a single alarm or several. If your mouth is open in a big yawn, it may be time for bed.

Ben was a driver, and his electric car was a cherry red color he was proud of. He was also trying to save money for a new battery. At night he sat on the sofa with the electricity bill in his hands and tried to study the numbers.

"Could you please tell me how much electricity the house used yesterday?" he asked the assistant. "I'm trying to cut my bill, because I'm saving up for a battery."

The assistant understood that he wanted yesterday's total from the home energy meter. It said the house had used eighteen units, and that the car charger had used more than half of them. It offered to show him the cheapest hours to charge.

Ben said yes, and wrote the times on the back of the bill.

Grace was not good with technology, and the kitchen speaker was new. Guests were coming in an hour, and she wanted to vacuum the rug first. Her recipe folder lay open on the table, and a cake was in the oven.

"Set a timer for ten minutes," she said. Then she looked at the cake. "No, wait. Make it fifteen."

The speaker understood that she wanted to change the number. It cancelled the ten minute timer and started a new one for fifteen minutes. It said plainly that the timer was now set for fifteen minutes.

Grace nodded. She felt lucky that it had listened to her second answer and not her first. She turned on the vacuum, and when the timer rang, the cake was done.

The person wants milk put on the shopping list.
mlik on the list
add milk to my shopping list
We're out of milk.
Put milk on the list, please.
Draw up the list for the weekend shop and put milk first.
I have a gift card for the big shop, so put milk on that list.
I'm almost home and there's no milk in the fridge, so remember it for the next shop.
Could you please write milk down so I don't forget it when I go to the shop tomorrow?

name: save_contact
does: Saves a person's name, phone number and address in your contacts.
inputs: the person's name and the details you want to keep
people say:
- Keep Dana's number: 555 0142
- Start a new entry for my dentist
- Write down the address for Uncle Joe, 14 Mill Road
- Remember my neighbour's phone number for me
- Put the new number in for my mum, the one I call most

name: find_lost_pet_posts
does: Looks for notices about lost or found pets near your home.
inputs: the kind of pet and the area you are looking in
people say:
- Has anyone seen a gray cat near Oak Street?
- Our dog got out, can you check the neighbourhood board?
- Did somebody find a medium dog with brown ears?
- Start looking for my lost rabbit, he is about knee height with a white tail
- Is there any news about the cat that went missing last week?

Person: I'm on the bus and the screen is too bright.
Assistant: I can fix that. Is it your phone or your tablet?
Person: The tablet. My hands are cold, so please be quick.
Assistant: How bright would you like it?
Person: About twenty-five percent.
Assistant: Done. The screen is at twenty-five percent now.
Person: Thank you. Can you also convert my old photos into paintings?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't do that. I can sort them into an album for you, though.

The person wants to know how many days are left until Tuesday.
days til tuesday?
How many sleeps until Tuesday?
Is Tuesday close?
How many days til tusday?
Count the days to Tuesday for me.
Can you scan my calendar and tell me how many days are left before Tuesday?
Is it a normal three days to Tuesday from now?
I would like to know how long I have to finish my work before Tuesday morning, so how many days are left?

Ana had just moved to the city for a new job. Her desk at the office was bare, and she wanted something tidy. She sat on her bed with her phone.

"Order a desk lamp," she said to the assistant. Then she stopped. "No, I mean a desk organizer. The lamp can wait."

The assistant understood that she had changed her mind. It dropped the lamp and searched for desk organizers. It found a wooden one that could be delivered on Thursday. Ana asked how to spell the name of the shop, because she wanted to tell her sister. The assistant spelled it out, letter by letter.

Ana confirmed the order, and the assistant said plainly that one wooden organizer would arrive on Thursday.

Birthdays are easy to forget, so most people write them down. A calendar app can keep the date and give you a reminder. People change the reminder with words like, tell me a week early, or make it repeat every year. They ask for gift ideas too, such as, what can I give a man who likes fishing? Some people want a card as well, and they say, help me organize cards for all my cousins.

A red mark on the calendar makes a birthday easy to see. If the date changes, you can say, move Dan's birthday to the fourth. If you no longer need it, you can say, remove the reminder.

A notes app is a place to keep ideas so you do not lose them. Some people prefer to type, and others like to speak. A voice note is a short recording that the phone can turn into words. At night a thought can come, and you can say, make a note: buy stamps. Later you can say, find my note about the wifi password, or read me my last note.

The app works well when notes have a short name. People change notes with words like, add milk to the shopping note, or delete the old one. They also say, put this note at the top, when they want to find it fast.

Person: Start the coffee maker and play the news.
Assistant: Sure. How strong would you like the coffee?
Person: Strong, I just finished a night shift. Can you repeat the strength options?
Assistant: There are three: mild, medium and strong.
Person: Strong, please. Also, can you order more beans online?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't order things online. I can put coffee beans on your shopping list, though.
Person: Good idea. And read me my email when the coffee is ready.
Assistant: I'll start the coffee now and tell you when it is ready.

Grandpa Harold had taken a nice walk through the forest park. When he came back to the gate, he could not remember where he had left the car. He took out his phone and spoke to it slowly.

"Tell me where I parked the car. No, wait. I mean tell me where the car is, not where I parked it last week."

The assistant understood that he wanted the place where the car was right now. It looked at the last spot his phone had saved and said that the car was in the second row of the north car park, near the picnic tables. It showed the place on the map.

Harold watched his step and followed the little dot all the way to the car.

Things at home wear out, and a repair is easier when you plan it. A filter in a heater or a fan needs a change every few months. People say, remind me to change the filter every three months. If something breaks, they say, book a plumber for Thursday, and they tell the shop what is wrong, how deep the leak is, or where it started. Someone with a broken favourite kettle might say, find me a repair shop near home.

A reminder helps you put the job on the calendar. You can change it with words like, make it earlier, or move it to next month.

Walter was not good with technology, but he wanted to write a letter to his neighbour. The neighbour's dog was noisy, and Walter had also borrowed some butter and wanted to say thank you. He sat in front of the screen and spoke in a careful voice.

"Please fix my spelling and tell me how many words are in this letter," he said. He did not know if the assistant would understand.

It did. It fixed three words and said that the letter had forty-two words. It also said it had left the kind parts as they were.

Walter nodded. He read the letter once more, printed it, and walked next door to put it in the mailbox.

Jo was a busy parent, and the children were hungry. Dinner was not ready, and the lawn needed water. A wire fence ran along one side of the garden, and the kids were learning to ride their bikes beside it.

"Run the sprinklers for half the time today," Jo said to the assistant. "It rained a little this morning, so we don't need the full time."

The assistant understood that she wanted the usual time cut in half. The sprinklers normally ran for twenty minutes, so it set them to run for ten. It said plainly that it had made the change for today only and that tomorrow they would go back to twenty minutes.

Jo thanked it and went to make dinner.

Mia was sixteen, and she had to be at school early for a concert tomorrow. She could not find a place to park her little red car near the hall. She sat on the stairs, dug a few coins from her bag, and typed to the assistant.

"need a parking spot near the school tomorrow at seven"

The assistant understood that she wanted a car park close to the school for the next morning at seven. It found one two streets away with a lot of free spaces and said it opened at half past six. It offered to remind her to leave early.

Mia said yes. She asked the assistant to upload the map of the car park to her phone so that she could find it fast. The assistant saved it, and she put her coins back in her bag.

The person wants the robot vacuum to start cleaning.
Start cleaning.
Vacuum the floor.
Send the robot out.
The floor is covered in crumbs.
We're leaving in the van in a minute, so let the vacuum do the house while we're out.
The dog climbed on the sofa with muddy paws, and now the rug is a mess.
Please run the robot while the kids are out, and keep it on silent mode so the baby can sleep.
Could you ask the little machine to go round the kitchen and the hall? I'm too tired to do it myself.

The person wants to know when their flight leaves.
When does my flight leave?
Departure time?
What time do I need to be at the airport, and which gate is it?
Is flight 212 on time?
Any tip on when boarding starts?
I have only a few hours before I leave, so when is my flight?
Could you please tell me what time the Lisbon flight takes off, and is it delayed?
Please lower my worry and tell me if the plane is leaving on time.

A scorekeeper is useful for board games, because people forget the numbers. It tells everyone who is winning and when the game is over. Players say things like, start a ten minute timer, add five points for Sam, or undo that, I pressed the wrong one. They also ask, who is winning?

In a game with a ladder, players climb up the board, and the scores can change fast. A family may play downstairs on a rainy day with a melon-shaped timer on the table. When the timer rings, the game stops, and someone says, read me the scores. If the rules are unclear, you can say, what is the rule for ties?

A focus timer helps you work without getting tired. A common way is to work for twenty-five minutes and then rest for five. People say, start a focus timer, make the break longer, or skip this break. A routine is a list of things you do at the same time every day, such as wake up, train, eat breakfast and begin work.

A healthy routine includes short breaks. Some people sit by the fireplace with a cup of tea, and others walk around the block. You can tell your assistant, remind me to stand up every hour, or change my break to ten minutes. If the timer is too short, you can say, make it longer.

Arthur was not good with technology, but he had a newspaper in his lap and a plan for Friday. He wanted to eat out and still sleep well afterwards. He talked to the speaker slowly.

"I can't hear a thing in the loud places," he said. "I would like to eat early on Friday somewhere calm."

The assistant understood that Arthur wanted a quiet restaurant and an early table. It looked for places with good reviews for being calm, and it found a small restaurant by the river that opened at five. It asked if he wanted a table for one, and Arthur said two, because his sister would come.

The assistant booked a table for two at five o'clock on Friday and read the address aloud.

The person wants a short workout they can do at home.
Give me a workout.
Quick routine, please.
What should I do for exercise today?
Something to build my legs.
Any new exercises for my back?
What's the first step if I want to start working out again?
Could you please suggest a gentle twenty minute workout I can do at home? I'm starting again after a sore knee, and I don't want to hurt it, so nothing with jumping.

Lena was an office worker, and it was almost noon. Her desk was full of papers, and she had not read the manual for the new lunch app. The phone was the only thing she wanted to talk to.

"Usual lunch," she said.

The assistant understood that she wanted the same lunch she had ordered most days, a chicken salad from the cafe across the road. It said so, and asked if she wanted to change anything. Lena said no, but she wanted the weight of the bag to be small, so that nothing would spill. The assistant put a note on the order.

It said the lunch would come in twenty minutes. Lena went back to her papers and was ready when the bell rang.

Homework is work from school that you finish at home. Each assignment has a subject and a due date. A phone or speaker can keep a list, so you know what is next. Students say things like, add a math test on Friday, what is due next week, or move my essay to Monday.

Some people ask for a reminder the evening before, and others ask for a study timer. A student with a trip to a field for science class might say, remind me to bring my boots. When a job is done, you can say, mark it finished. If a teacher changes the date, you can say, change the due date to Thursday.
